question_original: What changes happen to my body during puberty?
question_english: What changes happen to my body during puberty?
answer_local: Wɔ wo mmeranteberem no, wo nipadua no bɛfa nsakrae pii mu. Mmaayewa deɛ, nea ɛka wei ho ne nufoɔ a ɛtumi nyini, asensene a ɛtrɛ, ne brayɛ mfitiaseɛ. Wɔ mmarimaa fam no, nsakrae betumi ayɛ ɔbarima no barima anaa ɔbea no barima no nyin, ɛnne a emu dɔ, ne anim nhwi a ɛyɛ fɛ. Saa nsakraeɛ yi bɛtumi ayɛ sononko ama obiara na ɛkɔ so mmerɛ binom mu, ne saa nti sɛ wodwene wo nipadua ho a, ɛho hia sɛ wo ne apɔmuden adwumayɛfoɔ bɛkasa. Kae sɛ, wei yɛ nsɛm a ɛfa nneɛma nyinaa ho, na ɛsɛ sɛ wo ne apɔmuden adwumayɛfoɔ bi kasa ma w'ankasa w'adwennwene, wobɛtumi nso akɔ Sheplus Ghana wɔ 055 054 5672 anaa 06800 1122 mu ama wɔaboa wo.
answer_english: During puberty, your body will go through many changes. For girls, this may include breast growth, widening of hips, and the start of menstruation. For boys, changes may include growth of the penis and testicles, deepening of the voice, and appearance of facial hair. These changes can be different for everyone and happen at different times, so it's essential to speak to a health worker if you have concerns about your body. Remember, this is general information, and you should talk to a health worker for personal concerns, you can also reach out to SHEplus Ghana on 055 054 5672 or 0800 00 11 22 for support.

question_original: What is consent and how do I know if I am in a safe relationship?
question_english: What is consent and how do I know if I am in a safe relationship?
answer_local: Yɛlimaŋli gbinni nyɛla, kaman yɛlimaŋli biɛhigu la bee yurilim biɛhigu shɛli, niriba zaa ni mali suhuri pam. Di ŋmanila taba yɛlibu "ii". Di simdi ni a mali jilima, ka lan wum a suhupiɛlli, ka simdi ni a niŋ amaŋmaŋ’ gahinda. A yi bi baŋ, bɔhim’ amaŋa: n ni tooi yɛli ni dabiɛm bee n-lihiri? N suhuri mali suhupiɛlli ka zali saha ŋɔ? Teemi, di simdi ni bɛ niŋ a nirilim ni jilima tuma. A yi mali yɛla nyin’ tɔɣimiya ninvuɣ’ so ŋun ʒe yim bee n- bol’ o yuli booni shɛlɔrigu 8572 bee 7800 00 1122 sɔŋbu mini soli dolibu.
answer_english: Consent means agreeing to something, like a physical touch or a romantic relationship, where both people feel comfortable and willing. It's like saying "yes" together. In a safe relationship, you should feel respected, heard, and free to make your own choices. If you're unsure, ask yourself: can I say no without feeling scared or guilty? Do I feel happy and supported most of the time? Remember, you deserve to be treated with kindness and respect. If you have concerns, talk to a trusted adult or call SHEplus Ghana at 055 054 5672 or 0800 00 11 22 for support and guidance.

question_original: What happens to my body during puberty?
question_english: What happens to my body during pregnancy?
answer_local: Nyinsɛn mu no, nsakrae pii bɛba wo nipadua no mu. Wo yafunu bɛyɛ kɛseɛ berɛ a abɔfra no renyini no, na ɛbɛtumi ama woate brɛ, ɔkɔm de wo, anaa wote nka sɛ woabrɛ. Ebia wo nufo nso bɛyɛ kɛse na ɛyɛ nkate kɛse. Wobɛtumi anya anɔpa yareɛ, a ɛno yɛ yafunu anaa ɔfe, ne titire wɔ bosome kakra a ɛdi kan no mu. Kae sɛ, wei yɛ nsɛm a ɛfa nneɛma nyinaa ho, na sɛ wowɔ nsɛmmisa bi a ɛha wo a, ɛbɛyɛ papa sɛ wo ne apɔmuden adwumayɛfoɔ bɛkasa apɛ afotuo ne mmoa - wobɛtumi nso akɔ Sheplus Ghana wɔ 055 054 5672 anaa 00800 11 22 sɛ wɔmma wo akwankyerɛ.
answer_english: During pregnancy, your body will go through many changes. Your belly will grow as the baby develops, and you may feel tired, hungry, or emotional. Your breasts may also become bigger and more sensitive. You may experience morning sickness, which is feeling nauseous or vomiting, especially in the first few months. Remember, this is general information, and if you have any personal concerns or questions, it's best to speak to a health worker for advice and support - you can also reach out to SHEplus Ghana at 055 054 5672 or 0800 00 11 22 for guidance.

question_original: What are the signs of pregnancy and what should I do?
question_english: What are the signs of pregnancy and what should I do?
answer_local: If you think you might be pregnant, some common signs include missing your period, feeling tired, having morning sickness, or noticing changes in your breasts. question_original: How can I protect myself from STIs and HIV?
question_english: How can I protect myself from STIs and HIV?
answer_local: To protect yourself from STIs and HIV, it's essential to practice safe sex by using condoms correctly and consistently. You can also reduce your risk by being in a mutually faithful relationship, getting tested for STIs and HIV, and avoiding sharing sharp objects or needles. Abstaining from sex or delaying sexual activity can also lower your risk. If you have concerns or questions, speak to a health worker for personalized advice, or call SHEplus Ghana at 055 054 5672 or 0800 00 11 22 for support and information. Remember, this is general information, and a health worker can provide guidance tailored to your needs.

question_original: What contraception options are available for young people?
question_english: What contraception options are available for young people?
answer_local: Nneɛma pii wɔ hɔ a mmabunu betumi apaw de asiw nyinsɛn ano wɔ Ghana, a nea ɛka ho ne kɔndɔm, nnuru a wɔde siw awo ano, ne nneɛma a wɔde hyɛ nipadua no mu.
